Question 1

A body of mass 4kg is moving in a straight line along the x-axis under the action of a single force F, measured in Newtons. At time t seconds, the position of the body is given by s(t)=sin⁡t+t2 meters. Find the expression for the force acting on the body at time t.

a
2−cos⁡t
b
8+8cos⁡t
c
8−4sin⁡t
d
8+4sin⁡t
e
2+cos⁡t
Submit

decision.explanation: Acceleration is the second derivative of position: s''(t)=2−sin(t). Newton's second law gives F(t)=4s''(t)=8−4sin(t) newtons.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:
A body of mass $4\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons.
At time $t$ seconds, the position of the body is given by $s(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{t}^{2}$ meters.
Find the expression for the force acting on the body at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law

$$
F=ma,
$$

 
where $F$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a$ is the acceleration.

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{t}^{2}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡t+2t\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+2t) \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t+2 \\  & =2-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force in Newtons, is

$$
\begin{aligned}F & =ma \\  & =4\cdot (2-\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =8-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
A body of mass $64\,\text{kg}$ is moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis under the action of a single force $F,$ measured in Newtons $(\text{N}).$  At time $t>0$ seconds, the position of the body is given by $s(t)=\sqrt{t}$ meters.

Calculate the magnitude of the force at time $t=4$ seconds. Do not round the answer.

The magnitude of the force equals
{{field-1}} $\text{N}.$
after.worked_solution:
According to Newton’s second law,

$$
F(t)=ma(t),
$$

 
where $F(t)$ is the force, $m$ is the mass, and $a(t)$ is the acceleration.

To find the velocity $v(t),$ we differentiate the displacement $s(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{t}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{1/2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{t}^{-1/2}\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration $a(t),$ we differentiate the velocity $v(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{2}{t}^{-1/2}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}{t}^{-3/2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4{(\sqrt{t})}^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, the acceleration at $t=4\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}a(4) & =-\frac{1}{4{(\sqrt{4})}^{3}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4({2}^{3})} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4\cdot 8} \\  & =-\frac{1}{32}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the force in Newtons is

$$
\begin{aligned}F(4) & =ma(4) \\  & =64\cdot -\frac{1}{32} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the magnitude of the force is

$$
|F(4)|=|-2|=2\,\text{N}.
$$

\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}\,[\frac{1}{4}{e}^{-2t}(13-6t-2{t}^{2})] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[{e}^{-2t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(13-6t-2{t}^{2})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-2t})\cdot (13-6t-2{t}^{2})] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[{e}^{-2t}(-6-4t)-2{e}^{-2t}(13-6t-2{t}^{2})] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{e}^{-2t}(-6-4t-26+12t+4{t}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{e}^{-2t}(4{t}^{2}+8t-32) \\  & ={e}^{-2t}({t}^{2}+2t-8)\end{aligned}
$$

Since the mass is always positive, the force has zero magnitude when the acceleration equals zero. So, we set $a(t)=0$ and solve for $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{-2t}({t}^{2}+2t-8) & =0 \\ {t}^{2}+2t-8 & =0 \\ (t+4)(t-2) & =0 \\ t & =-4,2\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t\ge 0,$ we disregard the negative solution. 

Therefore, the force has zero magnitude at ${t}_{∗}=2\,\text{s}.$
